newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kurds invade U.N. centre to protest Turk attack.
newsitem.headline: Kurds invade U.N. centre to protest Turk attack.

text.p: GENEVA, May 22 (Reuter) Some 200 Kurdish demonstrators occupied part of the United Nations' European headquarters in Geneva on Thursday, demanding international action to halt Turkey's offensive into northern Iraq.

After three hours of negotiations with U.N. officials, they voted to stay put unless the world body passed a resolution condemning the Turkish assault and sent its refugee agency UNHCR back to a camp in Iraq it abandoned in mid-March.

A U.N. spokesman said talks were continuing "to try to persuade them to leave the building peacefully". But Swiss police were reported standing by ready to intervene if U.N. officials asked them to remove the Kurds.

The protesters, mainly men but including some women and children, rushed past security guards at the main gate and forced their way into the Palais des Nations overlooking Lake Geneva, smashing glass doors in the 1930s complex.
"We are demanding action by the United Nations and the international community to halt the massacre of our people in northern Iraq," said a demonstrator who identified himself as Argun Leman.

"The Turks have killed over 100 civilians, including many women and children. Why is nothing being done to stop them?" He said condemnation of the Turkish action by U.N. Secretary- General Kofi Annan was "not enough for us".

But later a protest spokeswoman, Elif Aktas, said the demonstrators also wanted a pledge by the UNHCR to return to the Atrush refugee camp in northern Iraq, where many Kurds from Turkey lived, before they would leave the building.

The agency halted operations in Atrush because it had been effectively taken over by the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), which is in conflict with another main faction, the Iraq-based Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).
Reports from the region on Thursday said Turkish troops were now installed in Atrush.

The demonstrators occupied a hall normally used as the reception area for high-level visitors to the Palais, chanting slogans in support of Kurdish independence, brandishing red, yellow and green PKK flags and banners and dancing.

One banner read: "War for Kuwait, Silence for Kurdistan. Why the Double Game?" Leman said the protesters wanted intervention similar to the U.S.-led action in northern Iraq in 1991 to protect Kurds against Iraqi forces.
"If they occupy our country, we occupy the United Nations," said one young demonstrator wearing a baseball cap. "We have no patience any more."

A delegation of protesters was received by Mohammed Sebti, the Moroccan administration chief for the U.N.'s Geneva office, a top legal officer and officials of the U.N. Human Rights Centre in the sprawling 1930s complex.

U.N. spokesman Jamel Ben Yamed said the protesters, from all over Switzerland, had been told they could formally present their complaints for forwarding to U.N. headquarters in New York if they left the building.
More than 10,000 Turkish troops, allied with the KDP, poured into northern Iraq last week in pursuit of PKK activists, who want a separate state in Turkey and operate out of the border region.

On Thursday, the troops were 200 km (125 miles) inside Iraq on a nine-day offensive. Many of Turkey's Western allies have criticised the action, in which Ankara says 1,446 PKK fighters have been killed.

Swiss police said they were in contact with the U.N. authorities but could not intervene without a formal request from officials of the world body. However, police sources said a riot squad was on standby.
